source.title: Dynamic Low-rank Approximation of Full-Matrix Preconditioner for Training Generalized Linear Models
source.authors: Tatyana Matveeva; Aleksandr Katrutsa; Evgeny Frolov

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Reports held-out test loss and accuracy when comparing adaptive optimizers with SGD and other baselines on synthetic and UCI logistic-regression tasks, extending optimizer generalization comparisons to these settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer comparisons on held-out test metrics. Synthetic-data curves are figure-only; real-dataset result statements summarize the proposed AdaGram variants against baselines without giving per-optimizer numerical values in the text.
record.test_reason: The study benchmarks a proposed optimizer on synthetic and UCI logistic-regression tasks. It does not test V4's image or language setting under limited learning-rate and schedule tuning: it tunes batch size, learning rate and epsilon, plus rank and memory for AdaGram, selecting configurations by final objective value. Its optimizer-performance comparisons do not test any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that AdaGram efficiently implements full-matrix adaptive preconditioning, with promising logistic-regression results motivating evaluation on more complex architectures and broader tasks.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates a proposed full-matrix adaptive optimizer on logistic-regression GLMs and compares it with SGD, diagonal AdaGrad, Shampoo, and KATE; it does not reproduce the cited optimizer-generalization studies.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature-correlation structure changes relative optimizer performance in the synthetic experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: On synthetic logistic-regression tasks, AdaGram loses to simpler optimizers on isotropic features and reaches lower final test loss with complex feature correlations, according to Section 4.3 and Figure 2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature correlations affect the relative convergence and held-out performance of full-matrix adaptive optimizers in logistic regression.

fits_no_version.finding: On Heart, Australian and Splice, the authors report comparable or better test loss and final accuracy for AdaGram variants versus baselines, including SGD, with little time overhead (Section 4.4, Figures 3–4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: With the study's hyperparameter searches, low-rank AdaGram can match or outperform baseline optimizers on UCI logistic-regression tasks.

record.problems: Test-loss and accuracy comparisons are presented mainly in plots, without numerical values or uncertainty estimates in the text. The real-dataset statements aggregate AdaGram variants against baselines rather than specifying each optimizer's result.
record.rows_left_out: No rows extracted: the text does not report optimizer-specific numerical values or distinct conditions in a form that can be assigned to individual methods. Figure 2 gives synthetic test-loss curves; Figures 3 and 4 give real-dataset test-loss and test-accuracy curves.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting alongside natural-label generalization and chance performance on held-out random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD generalization on image or language benchmarks under limited tuning, and the specified broader-tuning, weight-decay and optimizer-switching conditions.
Large-batch penalties under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove them.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across data sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking generalization gaps among similarly fitted convolutional networks.
Test-accuracy effects of removing memorized versus randomly selected training examples.

record.verdict_notes: There are no extracted rows to fix. The figure-only optimizer comparisons are already declared in rows_left_out. Their omission does not establish missing evidence for a claim version, and the reported superiority of AdaGram does not warrant a V4 verdict.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.

The reported figures compare AdaGram variants with adaptive and non-adaptive baselines on synthetic and UCI logistic-regression tasks, but the text does not give separate results for each optimizer. The study does not test image-classification or language benchmarks, Adam, equal training performance, or broader tuning.
Large-batch comparisons at fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Discusses adaptive optimization versus SGD and reports AdaGram performance, without testing or relying on the claimed generalization disadvantage.

tranche.reason: Sections 4.1–4.4 benchmark optimizer convergence on synthetic and UCI logistic-regression tasks. They neither test nor use any listed claim version; V4's image/language setting and limited tuning are untested.

source_check.notes: No rows, tagged statements or verdicts are listed. The authors-conclusion paraphrase matches Section 5; Section 4.2 selects configurations by final training objective after tuning batch size, learning rate, epsilon and additional AdaGram parameters.
